title: Path with Maximum Probability
summary: Given an undirected weighted graph with n nodes, where each edge has a probability of success associated with it, find the path from a specified start node to an end node that has the maximum probability of success.
statement: Given an undirected weighted graph with n nodes, where each edge has a probability of success associated with it, find the path from a specified start node to an end node that has the maximum probability of success. Return the probability of this path. If no path exists from the start node to the end node, return 0. The answer will be considered correct if it differs from the actual maximum probability by no more than 1e-5.
constraints: Each undirected edge has an independent traversal success probability.
Return the maximum product probability from start to end, or zero if unreachable.
hints: Use a max-priority queue keyed by best probability reached so far.
Relax an edge by multiplying the current path probability by its edge probability.
Keep a neighbor only when the product improves its best known value.
Because multiplying by values at most one never increases a path probability, the first queue removal of a node is optimal, as in Dijkstra’s proof.
